newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says arms on disputed islands defensive.
newsitem.headline: Iran says arms on disputed islands defensive.

text.p: Iran on Monday rejected an Arab statement blasting Tehran for allegedly deploying missiles on disputed Gulf islands and said Iranian military "measures" were defensive.

"The Islamic Republic of Iran will take any necessary measures inside its territory, including on the three Iranian Persian Gulf islands of Abu Musa and the Lesser and Greater Tunbs, to defend its territorial integrity," Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati told reporters.

Velayati was commenting on a strongly worded statement on Sunday by the Damascus Declaration states -- Egypt, Syria and the six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) -- which said Iran had deployed missiles in the islands, posing a direct threat to Gulf Arab states.
"The measures we are taking...are neither offensive nor expansionistic at all. They are purely defensive, which is the right of every country," Velayati said. He did not refer directly to missiles.

The Arab statement also demanded that Iran withdraw from the islands in favour of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), which also claims them. The islands lie close to major shipping lanes and have been at the centre of a dispute between the two Gulf states since 1992.
Velayati called the statement "damaging to regional cooperation".
"They (Arabs) create imaginary enemies for themselves in order to cover up their weakness against the Zionist regime (Israel)," Velayati said.
The members of the GCC are Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

They signed the Damascus Declaration with Egypt and Syria, a close ally of Iran, after the Gulf War over Kuwait in 1991. The foreign ministers of the eight countries meet twice a year to keep the alliance alive.
